The quality patterns below (adversarial verify, multi-modal sweep, completeness critic, loop-until-dry) are the tools; pick what fits the task. Lean toward orchestrating with workflows and adversarially verifying your findings — unless the work is trivial or already verified. Solo only on conversational turns or trivial mechanical edits. When a reminder says ultracode is off, revert to the opt-in rule in the Workflow tool description.

Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first. Every invocation automatically persists its script to a file under the session directory and returns the path in the tool result. To iterate on a workflow, edit that file with Write/Edit and re-invoke Workflow with `{scriptPath: "<path>"}` instead of resending the full script.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'find-flaky-tests',
    description: 'Find flaky tests and propose fixes',   // one-line, shown in permission dialog
    phases: [                                            // one entry per phase() call
      { title: 'Scan', detail: 'grep test logs for retries' },
      { title: 'Fix', detail: 'one agent per flaky test' },
    ],
  }
  // script body starts here — use agent()/parallel()/pipeline()/phase()/log()
  phase('Scan')
  const flaky = await agent('grep CI logs for retry markers', {schema: FLAKY_SCHEMA})
  ...

The `meta` object must be a PURE LITERAL — no variables, function calls, spreads, or template interpolation. Required fields: `name`, `description`. Optional: `whenToUse` (shown in the workflow list), `phases`. Use the SAME phase titles in meta.phases as in phase() calls — titles are matched exactly; a phase() call with no matching meta entry just gets its own progress group.

Script body hooks:
- agent(prompt: string, opts?: {label?: string, phase?: string, schema?: object, effort?: string, isolation?: 'worktree', agentType?: string}): Promise<any> — spawn a subagent. Without schema, returns its final text as a string. With schema (a JSON Schema), the subagent is forced to call a StructuredOutput tool and agent() returns the validated object — no parsing needed. Returns null if the user skips the agent mid-run or the subagent dies on a terminal API error after retries (filter with .filter(Boolean)). opts.label overrides the display label. opts.phase explicitly assigns this agent to a progress group (use this inside pipeline()/parallel() stages to avoid races on the global phase() state — same phase string → same group box). opts.effort overrides the reasoning effort for this agent call ('low' | 'medium' | 'high' | 'xhigh' | 'max') — omit to inherit the session effort; use 'low' for cheap mechanical stages and higher tiers only for the hardest verify/judge stages. opts.isolation: 'worktree' runs the agent in a fresh git worktree — EXPENSIVE (~200-500ms setup + disk per agent), use ONLY when agents mutate files in parallel and would otherwise conflict; the worktree is auto-removed if unchanged. opts.agentType uses a custom subagent type (e.g. 'general-purpose', 'code-reviewer') instead of the default workflow subagent — resolved from the same registry as the Agent tool; composes with schema (the custom agent's system prompt gets a StructuredOutput instruction appended).
- pipeline(items, stage1, stage2, ...): Promise<any[]> — run each item through all stages independently, NO barrier between stages. Item A can be in stage 3 while item B is still in stage 1. This is the DEFAULT for multi-stage work. Wall-clock = slowest single-item chain, not sum-of-slowest-per-stage. Every stage callback receives (prevResult, originalItem, index) — use originalItem/index in later stages to label work without threading context through stage 1's return value. A stage that throws drops that item to `null` and skips its remaining stages.
- parallel(thunks: Array<() => Promise<any>>): Promise<any[]> — run tasks concurrently. This is a BARRIER: awaits all thunks before returning. A thunk that throws (or whose agent errors) resolves to `null` in the result array — the call itself never rejects, so `.filter(Boolean)` before using the results. Use ONLY when you genuinely need all results together.
- log(message: string): void — emit a progress message to the user (shown as a narrator line above the progress tree)
- phase(title: string): void — start a new phase; subsequent agent() calls are grouped under this title in the progress display
- args: any — the value passed as Workflow's `args` input, verbatim (undefined if not provided). Pass arrays/objects as actual JSON values in the tool call, NOT as a JSON-encoded string — `args: ["a.ts", "b.ts"]`, not `args: "[\"a.ts\", ...]"` (a stringified list reaches the script as one string, so `args.filter`/`args.map` throw). Use this to parameterize named workflows — e.g. pass a research question, target path, or config object directly instead of via a side-channel file.
- budget: {total: number|null, spent(): number, remaining(): number} — the turn's token target from the user's "+500k"-style directive. `budget.total` is null if no target was set. `budget.spent()` returns output tokens spent this turn across the main loop and all workflows — the pool is shared, not per-workflow. `budget.remaining()` returns `max(0, total - spent())`, or `Infinity` if no target. The target is a HARD ceiling, not advisory: once `spent()` reaches `total`, further `agent()` calls throw. Use for dynamic loops: `while (budget.total && budget.remaining() > 50_000) { ... }`, or static scaling: `const FLEET = budget.total ? Math.floor(budget.total / 100_000) : 5`.
- workflow(nameOrRef: string | {scriptPath: string}, args?: any): Promise<any> — run another workflow inline as a sub-step and return whatever it returns. Pass a name to invoke a saved workflow (same registry as {name: "..."}), or {scriptPath} to run a script file you Wrote earlier. The child shares this run's concurrency cap, agent counter, abort signal, and token budget — its agents appear under a "▸ name" group in /workflows and its tokens count toward budget.spent(). The args param becomes the child's `args` global. Nesting is one level only: workflow() inside a child throws. Throws on unknown name / unreadable scriptPath / child syntax error; catch to handle gracefully.

Subagents are told their final text IS the return value (not a human-facing message), so they return raw data. For structured output, use the schema option — validation happens at the tool-call layer so the model retries on mismatch.
Schemas need {type: 'object', properties: {...}} at root and required ⊆ properties; unsatisfiable ones throw at agent().

Workflow agents can reach all session-connected MCP tools via ToolSearch — schemas load on demand per agent. Caveat: interactively-authenticated MCP servers (e.g. claude.ai) may be absent in headless/cron runs.

Subagents get the same CLAUDE.md files injected at start that you did (except built-in agent types that omit them, such as Explore and Plan) — don't tell them to re-read those or paste their rules into the prompt; name the specific rule a stage needs, if any.

Scripts are plain JavaScript, NOT TypeScript — type annotations (`: string[]`), interfaces, and generics fail to parse. The script body runs in an async context — use await directly. Standard JS built-ins (JSON, Math, Array, etc.) are available — EXCEPT `Date.now()`/`Math.random()`/argless `new Date()`, which throw (they would break resume); pass timestamps in via `args`, stamp results after the workflow returns, and for randomness vary the agent prompt/label by index. No filesystem or Node.js API access.

DEFAULT TO pipeline(). Only reach for a barrier (parallel between stages) when you genuinely need ALL prior-stage results together.

A barrier is correct ONLY when stage N needs cross-item context from all of stage N-1:
- Dedup/merge across the full result set before expensive downstream work
- Early-exit if the total count is zero ("0 bugs found → skip verification entirely")
- Stage N's prompt references "the other findings" for comparison

A barrier is NOT justified by:
- "I need to flatten/map/filter first" — do it inside a pipeline stage: pipeline(items, stageA, r => transform([r]).flat(), stageB)
- "The stages are conceptually separate" — that's what pipeline() models. Separate stages ≠ synchronized stages.
- "It's cleaner code" — barrier latency is real. If 5 finders run and the slowest takes 3× the fastest, a barrier wastes 2/3 of the fast finders' idle time.

Smell test: if you wrote
  const a = await parallel(...)
  const b = transform(a)        // flatten, map, filter — no cross-item dependency
  const c = await parallel(b.map(...))
that middle transform doesn't need the barrier. Rewrite as a pipeline with the transform inside a stage. When in doubt: pipeline.

Concurrent agent() calls are capped at min(16, available CPUs - 2) per workflow — excess calls queue and run as slots free up. You can still pass 100 items to parallel()/pipeline() and they all complete; only ~10 run at any moment. Total agent count across a workflow's lifetime is capped at 1000 — a runaway-loop backstop set far above any real workflow. A single parallel()/pipeline() call accepts at most 4096 items; passing more is an explicit error, not a silent truncation.

When a barrier IS correct — dedup across all findings before expensive verification:
  const all = await parallel(DIMENSIONS.map(d => () => agent(d.prompt, {schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA})))
  const deduped = dedupeByFileAndLine(all.filter(Boolean).flatMap(r => r.findings))  // <-- genuinely needs ALL at once
  const verified = await parallel(deduped.map(f => () => agent(verifyPrompt(f), {schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})))

Loop-until-count pattern — accumulate to a target:
  const bugs = []
  while (bugs.length < 10) {
    const result = await agent("Find bugs in this codebase.", {schema: BUGS_SCHEMA})
    bugs.push(...result.bugs)
    log(`${bugs.length}/10 found`)
  }

Loop-until-budget pattern — scale depth to the user's "+500k" directive. Guard on budget.total: with no target set, remaining() is Infinity and the loop would run straight to the 1000-agent cap.
  const bugs = []
  while (budget.total && budget.remaining() > 50_000) {
    const result = await agent("Find bugs in this codebase.", {schema: BUGS_SCHEMA})
    bugs.push(...result.bugs)
    log(`${bugs.length} found, ${Math.round(budget.remaining()/1000)}k remaining`)
  }

Composing patterns — exhaustive review (find → dedup vs seen → diverse-lens panel → loop-until-dry):
  const seen = new Set(), confirmed = []
  let dry = 0
  while (dry < 2) {                                              // loop-until-dry
    const found = (await parallel(FINDERS.map(f => () =>          // barrier: collect all finders this round
      agent(f.prompt, {phase: 'Find', schema: BUGS})))).filter(Boolean).flatMap(r => r.bugs)
    const fresh = found.filter(b => !seen.has(key(b)))           // dedup vs ALL seen — plain code, not an agent
    if (!fresh.length) { dry++; continue }
    dry = 0; fresh.forEach(b => seen.add(key(b)))
    const judged = await parallel(fresh.map(b => () =>           // every fresh bug judged concurrently...
      parallel(['correctness','security','repro'].map(lens => () =>   // ...each by 3 distinct lenses
        agent(`Judge "${b.desc}" via the ${lens} lens — real?`, {phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT})))
        .then(vs => ({ b, real: vs.filter(Boolean).filter(v => v.real).length >= 2 }))))
    confirmed.push(...judged.filter(v => v.real).map(v => v.b))
  }
  return confirmed
  // dedup vs `seen`, NOT `confirmed` — else judge-rejected findings reappear every round and it never converges.

Quality patterns — common shapes; pick by task and compose freely:
- Adversarial verify: spawn N independent skeptics per finding, each prompted to REFUTE. Kill if ≥majority refute. Prevents plausible-but-wrong findings from surviving.
    const votes = await parallel(Array.from({length: 3}, () => () =>
      agent(`Try to refute: ${claim}. Default to refuted=true if uncertain.`, {schema: VERDICT})))
    const survives = votes.filter(Boolean).filter(v => !v.refuted).length >= 2
- Perspective-diverse verify: when a finding can fail in more than one way, give each verifier a distinct lens (correctness, security, perf, does-it-reproduce) instead of N identical refuters — diversity catches failure modes redundancy can't.
- Judge panel: generate N independent attempts from different angles (e.g. MVP-first, risk-first, user-first), score with parallel judges, synthesize from the winner while grafting the best ideas from runners-up. Beats one-attempt-iterated when the solution space is wide.
- Loop-until-dry: for unknown-size discovery (bugs, issues, edge cases), keep spawning finders until K consecutive rounds return nothing new. Simple counters (while count < N) miss the tail.
- Multi-modal sweep: parallel agents each searching a different way (by-container, by-content, by-entity, by-time). Each is blind to what the others surface; useful when one search angle won't find everything.
- Completeness critic: a final agent that asks "what's missing — modality not run, claim unverified, source unread?" What it finds becomes the next round of work.
- No silent caps: if a workflow bounds coverage (top-N, no-retry, sampling), `log()` what was dropped — silent truncation reads as "covered everything" when it didn't.

Scale to what the user asked for. "find any bugs" → a few finders, single-vote verify. "thoroughly audit this" or "be comprehensive" → larger finder pool, 3–5 vote adversarial pass, synthesis stage. When unsure, lean toward thoroughness for research/review/audit requests and toward brevity for quick checks.

These patterns aren't exhaustive — compose novel harnesses when the task calls for it (tournament brackets, self-repair loops, staged escalation, whatever fits).

Use this tool for multi-step orchestration where control flow should be deterministic (loops, conditionals, fan-out) rather than model-driven.

## Resume

The tool result includes a runId. To resume after a pause, kill, or script edit, relaunch with Workflow({scriptPath, resumeFromRunId}) — the longest unchanged prefix of agent() calls returns cached results instantly; the first edited/new call and everything after it runs live. Same script + same args → 100% cache hit. Before diagnosing why a completed workflow returned an empty or unexpected result, Read <transcriptDir>/journal.jsonl — it records each agent's actual return value; do not assume cached results are non-empty. Date.now()/Math.random()/new Date() are unavailable in scripts (they would break this) — stamp results after the workflow returns, or pass timestamps via args. Fallback when no journal is available: Read agent-<id>.jsonl files in the transcript directory and hand-author a continuation script.

This session has the default workflow size guideline: medium — keep workflows under 10 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale. The user can raise or remove it with "Dynamic workflow size" in /config.

script.description: Self-contained workflow script. Must begin with `export const meta = { name, description, phases }` (pure literal, no computed values) followed by the script body using agent()/parallel()/pipeline()/phase().

name.description: Name of a predefined workflow (built-in or from .claude/workflows/). Resolves to a self-contained script.

description.description: Ignored — set the workflow description in the script's `meta` block.

title.description: Ignored — set the workflow title in the script's `meta` block.

args.description: Optional input value exposed to the script as the global `args`, verbatim. Pass arrays/objects as actual JSON values, NOT as a JSON-encoded string — a stringified list breaks `args.filter`/`args.map` in the script. Use for parameterized named workflows (e.g. a research question).

scriptPath.description: Path to a workflow script file on disk. Every Workflow invocation persists its script under the session directory and returns the path in the tool result. To iterate, edit that file with Write/Edit and re-invoke Workflow with the same `scriptPath` instead of re-sending the full script. Takes precedence over `script` and `name`.

resumeFromRunId.description: Run ID of a prior Workflow invocation to resume from. Completed agent() calls with unchanged (prompt, opts) return their cached results instantly; only edited or new calls re-run. Same-session only. Stop the prior run first (TaskStop) before resuming.

25	// InputError reports a fatal problem with one physical input line.
26	type InputError struct {
27		Line   int
28		Reason string
29	}
30	
31	func (e *InputError) Error() string {
32		return fmt.Sprintf("line %d: %s", e.Line, e.Reason)
33	}

35	// OutputError reports that output triggered by one physical input line could
36	// not be written in full. Line is that input line (blank lines count), and
37	// Kind is either "window result" or "late-event notice". Detail identifies
38	// the record: a window's key and [start,end), or the skipped event time and
39	// the watermark used to judge it. Err is the writer's own error, including
40	// when only a prefix was accepted before it failed; when the writer reported
41	// no error but accepted too few bytes, Err is io.ErrShortWrite. Use
42	// errors.Is to inspect it. Content the writer already accepted stays in
43	// place and fully written earlier results stay valid.
44	type OutputError struct {
45		Line   int
46		Kind   string
47		Detail string
48		Err    error
49	}
50	
51	func (e *OutputError) Error() string {
52		return fmt.Sprintf("line %d: %s not fully written (%s): %v", e.Line, e.Kind, e.Detail, e.Err)
53	}

55	func (e *OutputError) Unwrap() error {
56		return e.Err
57	}

59	// writeFull writes all of p to w in one call. Any writer error is returned
60	// unchanged, even when the writer accepted a prefix first, so callers keep
61	// errors.Is access to the original error. A nil error with fewer than
62	// len(p) accepted bytes is reported as io.ErrShortWrite; writeFull never
63	// retries or resends the missing tail.
64	func writeFull(w io.Writer, p []byte) error {
65		n, err := w.Write(p)
66		if err != nil {
67			return err
68		}
69		if n < len(p) {
70			return io.ErrShortWrite
71		}
72		return nil
73	}

76	// *AggregateParamError reports.
77	type AggregateParamName string
78

81		AggregateParamWindow AggregateParamName = "window"
82		// AggregateParamSlide is the slide interval (--slide-ms).
83		AggregateParamSlide AggregateParamName = "slide"

89	// one parameter.
90	type AggregateParamKind string
91	
92	const (
93		// AggregateParamNotPositive means the value was zero or negative where a
94		// positive signed 64-bit integer is required.
95		AggregateParamNotPositive AggregateParamKind = "not_positive"
96		// AggregateParamTooLarge means the slide interval exceeds the window
97		// length. It is reported for AggregateParamSlide and carries the window
98		// length in Limit.
99		AggregateParamTooLarge AggregateParamKind = "too_large"
100	)

102	// AggregateParamError reports one invalid aggregate start parameter. It is the
103	// single source of the shared startup parameter limits: every aggregate entry
104	// point (the library runners and the command line) funnels its numeric
105	// parameter checks through ValidateAggregateParams, so the same restriction is
106	// stated in one place. Which parameter may be omitted, and what an omitted or
107	// zero value means, is entry-specific and decided by the caller; this reports
108	// only the limits common to every entry. Field identifies the parameter, Kind
109	// the violated limit, Value the rejected value and Limit the window length for
110	// AggregateParamTooLarge (zero otherwise). Error renders the library entry
111	// point's existing wording, which callers may rephrase for their own surface
112	// while keeping the field-driven decision identical.
113	type AggregateParamError struct {
114		Field AggregateParamName
115		Kind  AggregateParamKind
116		Value int64
117		Limit int64
118	}
119	
120	func (e *AggregateParamError) Error() string {
121		switch e.Kind {
122		case AggregateParamTooLarge:
123			return fmt.Sprintf("slide interval %d must not exceed window length %d", e.Value, e.Limit)
124		case AggregateParamNotPositive:
125			switch e.Field {
126			case AggregateParamWindow:
127				return fmt.Sprintf("window length must be a positive signed 64-bit integer, got %d", e.Value)
128			case AggregateParamSlide:
129				return fmt.Sprintf("slide interval must be a positive signed 64-bit integer, got %d", e.Value)
130			case AggregateParamPartitions:
131				return fmt.Sprintf("partition count must be a positive signed 64-bit integer, got %d", e.Value)
132			}
133		}
134		return fmt.Sprintf("invalid aggregate parameter %s: %d", e.Field, e.Value)
135	}

137	// ValidateAggregateParams enforces the aggregate startup limits shared by every
138	// entry point, in the order they have always been reported: window length,
139	// then slide interval, then the slide-vs-window comparison, then the partition
140	// count. windowMillis must be a positive signed 64-bit integer. slideMillis
141	// must be a positive signed 64-bit integer no greater than windowMillis; it
142	// does not have to divide windowMillis, and equality is the fixed-window case.
143	// partitions must not be negative; zero itself is accepted here because the
144	// library entry points use it to select legacy single-watermark mode -- an
145	// entry that rejects an explicitly supplied zero (the command line) keeps that
146	// policy of its own before or around this call. The first violated limit is
147	// returned as *AggregateParamError; nil means the parameters are sound and the
148	// caller may start reading input, so no invalid configuration ever reaches the
149	// input reader.
150	func ValidateAggregateParams(windowMillis, slideMillis, partitions int64) error {
151		if windowMillis <= 0 {
152			return &AggregateParamError{Field: AggregateParamWindow, Kind: AggregateParamNotPositive, Value: windowMillis}
153		}
154		if slideMillis <= 0 {
155			return &AggregateParamError{Field: AggregateParamSlide, Kind: AggregateParamNotPositive, Value: slideMillis}
156		}
157		if slideMillis > windowMillis {
158			return &AggregateParamError{Field: AggregateParamSlide, Kind: AggregateParamTooLarge, Value: slideMillis, Limit: windowMillis}
159		}
160		if partitions < 0 {
161			return &AggregateParamError{Field: AggregateParamPartitions, Kind: AggregateParamNotPositive, Value: partitions}
162		}
163		return nil
164	}

177	// RunAggregate reads line-delimited JSON records from r and writes closed
178	// fixed window results, one JSON object per line, to out. windowMillis must
179	// be a positive signed 64-bit integer. Windows are fixed-length, start at
180	// time zero and use a left-closed right-open interval. Closure is driven
181	// solely by input watermarks: a window whose end is less than or equal to the
182	// current watermark is emitted once, ordered by end ascending and then by key
183	// in UTF-8 byte order. Late events (event time below the current watermark)
184	// are reported on lateLog with their physical line number and skipped. Every
185	// output must land in full: a window result is its complete JSON object plus
186	// trailing newline and a late-event notice is its complete single line. If
187	// the corresponding writer returns an error after accepting zero bytes or
188	// only a prefix, or accepts too few bytes with no error, the run fails at
189	// once with *OutputError naming the triggering physical input line:
190	// window-result failures identify the key and window [start,end), and
191	// late-notice failures identify the skipped event time and the watermark
192	// used; a nil-error short write is io.ErrShortWrite and errors.Is exposes
193	// the writer's original error. After such a failure no further records are
194	// processed, the failed content is neither rewritten nor resent, and
195	// still-open windows produce no further results; content already accepted
196	// by the writers stays in place, including fully written earlier results.
197	// Fatal record problems return *InputError; results already written to out
198	// stay written, and open windows are not flushed at end of input. An event
199	// key that would lose characters when decoded -- invalid UTF-8 bytes, or a
200	// \u escape whose surrogate half is unpaired or mispaired -- is such a fatal
201	// problem: it is never repaired to U+FFFD and counted, so distinct damaged
202	// keys can never merge or collide with a key that is genuinely U+FFFD. The
203	// check runs before the late-event check, so a damaged key is fatal even
204	// below the current watermark.
205	//
206	// An event record may name its top-level field "key" at most once. The field
207	// is judged after JSON decoding, so writing key directly and writing it with
208	// an escape for the letter k (backslash-u-006b followed by ey, which decodes
209	// to key) are two spellings of the same field and a record carrying both is a
210	// duplicate; member order and equal values do not change that, and a "key"
211	// nested inside another member's object or array is not counted. Once the
212	// line has parsed as one complete JSON object and its type is event, the
213	// duplicate is fatal and is rejected before the key, time, value or
214	// partition fields are interpreted and before partition and watermark state
215	// is consulted: an empty or damaged earlier key, an event below the current
216	// watermark or an event for an idle partition is still reported as the
217	// duplicate rather than as a field error, a late notice or an idle-partition
218	// error. The event contributes no count or sum, no later record is read, and
219	// results already fully written to out stay written. A watermark or idle
220	// record that happens to carry a key keeps treating it as an ignored extra
221	// field. Lines that are not one complete JSON object keep their original
222	// invalid-JSON error instead.
223	//
224	// A read failure is distinct from reaching the end of input. Only a reader
225	// returning the bare io.EOF sentinel is a clean end, where a final record that
226	// arrived without a trailing newline is still processed (and a damaged one is
227	// an *InputError carrying its physical line number). A wrapped io.EOF or a
228	// combined error whose chain merely contains io.EOF is still a read failure.
229	// When r returns any error other than the bare io.EOF after delivering bytes,
230	// only records whose newline was already received are processed, in order,
231	// including records returned by the same Read that carried the error; the
232	// remaining unterminated bytes never become an event, watermark or idle
233	// declaration and can produce no late notice or window result, and the
234	// reader's own error is then returned unchanged so errors.Is exposes it. A
235	// record or output failure on one of those complete lines is reported
236	// instead of the read error discovered afterwards.
237	//
238	// This is the legacy single-watermark mode: records carry no partition field
239	// and any extra fields are ignored. Use RunAggregatePartitioned to merge
240	// several independent input sources of the same stream, or
241	// RunAggregateSliding to emit overlapping windows at a shorter interval.
242	func RunAggregate(r io.Reader, windowMillis int64, out io.Writer, lateLog io.Writer) error {
243		return RunAggregatePartitionedSliding(r, windowMillis, windowMillis, 0, out, lateLog)
244	}
245	
246	// RunAggregateSliding is RunAggregate with overlapping sliding windows. The
247	// window length is windowMillis and consecutive window starts are slideMillis
248	// apart, beginning at time zero: 0, slideMillis, 2*slideMillis, ... Each
249	// window is left-closed right-open and no window with a negative start is
250	// created. slideMillis must be a positive signed 64-bit integer no greater
251	// than windowMillis and does not have to divide it; slideMillis equal to
252	// windowMillis is exactly RunAggregate's fixed-window behavior. A valid event
253	// is counted once in every window that contains its event time, adding to
254	// that window's per-key count and the full value to its sum. Everything else
255	// (watermark-only closure, ordering, late reporting, overflow handling and
256	// end-of-input behavior) is identical to RunAggregate.
257	func RunAggregateSliding(r io.Reader, windowMillis, slideMillis int64, out io.Writer, lateLog io.Writer) error {
258		return RunAggregatePartitionedSliding(r, windowMillis, slideMillis, 0, out, lateLog)
259	}
260	
261	// RunAggregatePartitioned is RunAggregatePartitionedSliding with slideMillis
262	// equal to windowMillis (non-overlapping fixed windows).
263	func RunAggregatePartitioned(r io.Reader, windowMillis, partitions int64, out io.Writer, lateLog io.Writer) error {
264		return RunAggregatePartitionedSliding(r, windowMillis, windowMillis, partitions, out, lateLog)
265	}
266	
267	// RunAggregatePartitionedSliding combines sliding windows (see
268	// RunAggregateSliding) with partitioned inputs: events from different
269	// partitions merge into one count and sum per key and window, and both the
270	// late-event check and window closure use the effective (minimum) watermark.
271	// windowMillis and slideMillis are validated exactly as in
272	// RunAggregateSliding. partitions selects the input mode:
273	//
274	//   - partitions == 0: legacy single-watermark mode. Records do not carry a
275	//     partition field; any extra fields are ignored.
276	//
277	//   - partitions > 0: partitioned mode, merging partitions independent input
278	//     sources of the same stream. Every event and watermark record must carry
279	//     an integer "partition" in [0,partitions). Each partition advances its
280	//     own watermark; no effective watermark exists until every partition has
281	//     reported at least once, afterwards the effective watermark is the
282	//     minimum of the per-partition values. Window closure and late-event
283	//     checks use this minimum, so one partition's larger watermark can never
284	//     close a window or drop an event ahead of the others. A partition
285	//     watermark may repeat or jump forward but never move backwards.
286	//
287	//     A partition may be declared idle with
288	//     {"type":"idle","partition":p}. An idle partition stops contributing to
289	//     the effective watermark: non-idle partitions that have not reported a
290	//     watermark yet still keep the effective watermark unknown, while a
291	//     partition that never reported may itself be declared idle. When every
292	//     remaining (non-idle) partition has reported, the effective watermark is
293	//     their minimum and the idle record itself can close windows. If all
294	//     partitions are idle, the last produced effective watermark is retained;
295	//     when none was ever produced it stays unknown. Idleness is declared by
296	//     the input only, never inferred from time; a repeated idle declaration
297	//     is a no-op. The next watermark record for that partition resumes it:
298	//     its time must be at least both the partition's previous watermark and
299	//     the current effective watermark. An event for an idle partition is
300	//     fatal; it never resumes implicitly.
301	//
302	// partitions < 0 is an error. Windows, ordering, late-event reporting,
303	// overflow checks and end-of-input behavior are otherwise identical to
304	// RunAggregateSliding.
305	func RunAggregatePartitionedSliding(r io.Reader, windowMillis, slideMillis, partitions int64, out io.Writer, lateLog io.Writer) error {
306		if err := ValidateAggregateParams(windowMillis, slideMillis, partitions); err != nil {
307			return err
308		}
309		s := &aggregateState{
310			windowMillis:  windowMillis,
311			slideMillis:   slideMillis,
312			windows:       make(map[windowID]*windowState),
313			out:           out,
314			lateLog:       lateLog,
315			partitions:    partitions,
316			partWatermark: make(map[int64]*int64),
317			idle:          make(map[int64]bool),
318			// Every partition starts out active and unreported; in legacy mode
319			// (partitions == 0) the counter stays zero and is never consulted.
320			unreportedActive: partitions,
321		}
322	
323		// Read records with a line collector that keeps a read failure distinct
324		// from end of input: only newline-terminated lines (plus, at a clean EOF,
325		// one unterminated final line) ever become records.
326		lineNo := 0
327		err := readAggregateLines(r, func(line string, no int) error {
328			lineNo = no
329			if strings.TrimSpace(line) == "" {
330				return nil
331			}
332			return s.processLine(line, lineNo)
333		})
334		return err
335	}
336	
337	// maxAggregateLineBytes caps the size of a single physical input line, matching
338	// the scanner buffer limit this used to run with. A line this long is fatal
339	// before its record is parsed.
340	const maxAggregateLineBytes = 1024 * 1024 * 1024
341	
342	// errAggregateLineTooLong reports a physical input line that never ends within
343	// maxAggregateLineBytes.
344	var errAggregateLineTooLong = errors.New("aggregate input line longer than 1 GiB")
345	
346	// errAggregateBadReadCount reports an io.Reader that handed back a byte count
347	// outside the destination buffer, violating the io.Reader contract.
348	var errAggregateBadReadCount = errors.New("aggregate reader returned an impossible byte count")
349	
350	// readAggregateLines feeds newline-delimited physical lines from r to handle,
351	// counting every line (a bare "\n" is a blank line too) and stripping a single
352	// trailing '\r' so CRLF input works as before. Clean end of input and a
353	// non-EOF read failure are handled differently: only the bare io.EOF
354	// sentinel is a clean end, and then a final line missing its newline is still
355	// delivered, exactly like every other final record; a wrapped io.EOF or a
356	// combined error whose chain contains io.EOF is a failure, not an end. After
357	// any error other than the bare io.EOF only lines whose newline was already
358	// received (including those delivered by the same Read that carried the
359	// error) are handled, in order, and then the reader's original error is
360	// returned. The unterminated tail never reaches handle, so a read failure
361	// mid-record can neither be misreported as an input error nor produce
362	// events, watermarks, idle declarations, late notices or window results. A
363	// non-nil error from handle stops reading immediately and replaces the read
364	// error, so an earlier record or output failure is not overwritten by a
365	// failure the reader only reports later.
366	func readAggregateLines(r io.Reader, handle func(line string, lineNo int) error) error {
367		// buf[start:end] is the undelivered tail; buf[:start] is space freed by
368		// already delivered lines. The buffer is compacted and grown like
369		// bufio.Scanner's, so a long unterminated line is bounded by
370		// maxAggregateLineBytes instead of growing without limit.
371		//
372		// searchFrom is the earliest absolute index not yet inspected for a '\n':
373		// every byte before it has either been delivered or searched already. A
374		// Read can only introduce a newline in the bytes it just appended, so the
375		// pending tail of a long line is never rescanned; scanning, compaction and
376		// growth together stay linear in the cumulative byte count even when each
377		// Read brings a single byte. searchFrom >= start always holds, and
378		// compaction/growth shift every absolute index by the same start they do.
379		buf := make([]byte, 64*1024)
380		start, end := 0, 0
381		searchFrom := 0
382		lineNo := 0
383		emptyReads := 0
384		deliver := func(b []byte) error {
385			lineNo++
386			line := strings.TrimSuffix(string(b), "\r")
387			return handle(line, lineNo)
388		}
389		for {
390			// Move the pending tail to the front when its freed prefix is large
391			// enough or when the whole buffer is pending.
392			if start > 0 && (end == len(buf) || start > len(buf)/2) {
393				copy(buf, buf[start:end])
394				end -= start
395				searchFrom -= start
396				if searchFrom < 0 {
397					searchFrom = 0
398				}
399				start = 0
400			}
401			if end == len(buf) {
402				// No newline fit before the end: the physical line is too long.
403				if len(buf) >= maxAggregateLineBytes {
404					return errAggregateLineTooLong
405				}
406				newLen := len(buf) * 2
407				if newLen > maxAggregateLineBytes || newLen < len(buf) {
408					newLen = maxAggregateLineBytes
409				}
410				grown := make([]byte, newLen)
411				copy(grown, buf[start:end])
412				buf = grown
413				end -= start
414				searchFrom -= start
415				if searchFrom < 0 {
416					searchFrom = 0
417				}
418				start = 0
419			}
420			n, readErr := r.Read(buf[end:])
421			if n < 0 || n > len(buf)-end {
422				// A Reader must never report a byte count outside the buffer.
423				return errAggregateBadReadCount
424			}
425			end += n
426			// Only this Read's newly appended bytes can still hold an unseen
427			// newline; search from searchFrom rather than from start, so a long
428			// line delivered a few bytes at a time costs one scan of each byte
429			// instead of one scan per Read over the whole accumulated tail.
430			for searchFrom < end {
431				i := bytes.IndexByte(buf[searchFrom:end], '\n')
432				if i < 0 {
433					break
434				}
435				idx := searchFrom + i
436				if err := deliver(buf[start:idx]); err != nil {
437					return err
438				}
439				start = idx + 1
440				searchFrom = start
441			}
442			searchFrom = end
443			if readErr != nil {
444				if readErr == io.EOF {
445					// Clean end of input: a trailing line without a newline is a
446					// complete final record; an empty tail (input ending exactly
447					// on '\n') is nothing, not an extra blank line. Only the
448					// bare io.EOF sentinel counts -- a wrapped EOF or a combined
449					// error whose chain contains io.EOF is a read failure, never
450					// a clean end.
451					if end > start {
452						if err := deliver(buf[start:end]); err != nil {
453							return err
454						}
455					}
456					return nil
457				}
458				// Any other failure means the stream stopped mid-record: the
459				// still-unterminated bytes are not a record. Surface the original
460				// error unchanged so errors.Is keeps working for callers.
461				return readErr
462			}
463			if n == 0 {
464				// No data and no error: refuse to spin forever on a broken Reader.
465				emptyReads++
466				if emptyReads > 100 {
467					return io.ErrNoProgress
468				}
469			} else {
470				emptyReads = 0
471			}
472		}
473	}
474	
475	type aggregateState struct {
476		windowMillis int64
477		slideMillis  int64 // distance between consecutive window starts; equals windowMillis for fixed windows
478		windows      map[windowID]*windowState
479		out          io.Writer
480		lateLog      io.Writer
481	
482		partitions    int64 // 0 = legacy single-watermark mode
483		watermark     *int64
484		partWatermark map[int64]*int64 // partition -> last watermark; partitioned mode only
485		idle          map[int64]bool   // partitions declared idle in the input; partitioned mode only
486		// unreportedActive counts the partitions that are neither idle nor have
487		// reported a watermark yet; partitioned mode only. While it is positive
488		// no effective watermark exists, so the waiting check is a single look at
489		// this counter instead of a rescan of every partition's reporting state.
490		// It never increases: a partition leaves the count by reporting or by
491		// being declared idle, and resuming from idle always happens through a
492		// watermark record, which reports at the same moment.
493		unreportedActive int64
494	}
495	
496	func (s *aggregateState) processLine(line string, lineNo int) error {
497		// Parse with a streaming token decoder rather than into a map: a map
498		// silently keeps the last value of a repeated member name, while the
499		// scan additionally counts how many top-level members decode to "key".
500		obj, keyCount, err := scanAggregateObject(line)
501		if err != nil {
502			return &InputError{Line: lineNo, Reason: "invalid JSON record: " + err.Error()}
503		}
504	
505		typeRaw, ok := obj["type"]
506		if !ok {
507			return &InputError{Line: lineNo, Reason: `missing required string field "type"`}
508		}
509		recordType, err := decodeString(typeRaw, "type")
510		if err != nil {
511			return &InputError{Line: lineNo, Reason: err.Error()}
512		}
513	
514		switch recordType {
515		case "event":
516			// Once the JSON is complete and recognized as an event, a repeated
517			// top-level key is rejected before any event field is read or
518			// decoded: an empty or damaged earlier value or a legal later one
519			// never becomes a field error, a late-event notice or an
520			// idle-partition error.
521			if keyCount > 1 {
522				return &InputError{Line: lineNo, Reason: duplicateEventKeyReason}
523			}
524			return s.processEvent(obj, lineNo)
525		case "watermark":
526			return s.processWatermark(obj, lineNo)
527		case "idle":
528			// Only partitioned mode knows idle declarations; legacy
529			// single-watermark mode treats it as any unknown record type.
530			if s.partitions == 0 {
531				return &InputError{Line: lineNo, Reason: fmt.Sprintf("unknown record type %q", recordType)}
532			}
533			return s.processIdle(obj, lineNo)
534		default:
535			return &InputError{Line: lineNo, Reason: fmt.Sprintf("unknown record type %q", recordType)}
536		}
537	}
538	
539	// duplicateEventKeyReason is the record error for a complete event whose JSON
540	// object names the top-level field "key" more than once.
541	const duplicateEventKeyReason = `duplicate field "key": an event record must name "key" at most once at its top level`
542	
543	// scanAggregateObject parses one complete JSON object record the way the
544	// aggregate entries read it and additionally reports how many of the object's
545	// own members decode to the field name "key". Members are counted in JSON
546	// source order with their decoded names, so a member written "key" and one
547	// whose quoted name escapes the letter k (backslash-u-006b-ey, which JSON
548	// decodes to key) are the same field and both count, while a "key" nested
549	// inside another member's object or array is not top-level and is skipped
550	// wholesale by decoding that value. A non-object, malformed JSON or trailing
551	// data is rejected, and the reported error is re-derived from the existing
552	// json.Unmarshal-into-a-map parse so such input keeps its original invalid
553	// JSON wording; the duplicate-key rule therefore applies only to a record
554	// that parsed as one complete object. The returned map is exactly what that
555	// unmarshal produced (a repeated member keeps its last value); the count is
556	// what lets callers reject the repetition instead of silently using it.
557	func scanAggregateObject(line string) (map[string]json.RawMessage, int, error) {
558		dec := json.NewDecoder(strings.NewReader(line))
559		first, err := dec.Token()
560		if err != nil {
561			return nil, 0, invalidAggregateJSON(line)
562		}
563		delim, ok := first.(json.Delim)
564		if !ok || delim != '{' {
565			// Route every non-object opening through the legacy map parse, which
566			// decides its exact error wording -- and, for JSON null, no error at
567			// all: a null unmarshals into a nil map, so the caller reaches the
568			// missing-type report exactly as it did before the streaming scan.
569			return nil, 0, invalidAggregateJSON(line)
570		}
571		obj := make(map[string]json.RawMessage)
572		keyCount := 0
573		for dec.More() {
574			nameToken, err := dec.Token()
575			if err != nil {
576				return nil, 0, invalidAggregateJSON(line)
577			}
578			name := nameToken.(string) // between { and }, object member names are JSON strings
579			var raw json.RawMessage
580			if err := dec.Decode(&raw); err != nil {
581				return nil, 0, invalidAggregateJSON(line)
582			}
583			obj[name] = raw
584			if name == "key" {
585				keyCount++
586			}
587		}
588		if _, err := dec.Token(); err != nil { // the closing '}'
589			return nil, 0, invalidAggregateJSON(line)
590		}
591		// One complete object only: trailing JSON (unlike trailing whitespace) is
592		// malformed, as it was for json.Unmarshal.
593		if _, err := dec.Token(); err != io.EOF {
594			return nil, 0, invalidAggregateJSON(line)
595		}
596		return obj, keyCount, nil
597	}
598	
599	// invalidAggregateJSON re-runs the pre-existing map parse for a line the
600	// streaming object scan rejected as not one complete object, so malformed
601	// JSON keeps its original reason text exactly. It returns nil for JSON null,
602	// which unmarshals into a nil map without error; the caller treats that like
603	// any object with no "type" member and reports the missing type, preserving
604	// the old behavior for null.
605	func invalidAggregateJSON(line string) error {
606		var obj map[string]json.RawMessage
607		return json.Unmarshal([]byte(line), &obj)
608	}
609	
610	// floorDiv returns math.Floor(a/b) for b > 0; Go's / truncates toward zero,
611	// so negative numerators need explicit adjustment.
612	func floorDiv(a, b int64) int64 {
613		q := a / b
614		if a%b != 0 && a < 0 {
615			q--
616		}
617		return q
618	}
619	
620	// containingWindows describes every window that contains one event time, in
621	// one derivation shared by the normal counting path and the window-end
622	// overflow precheck: how many windows there are, where each starts, and which
623	// (if any) is the earliest whose end leaves the signed 64-bit range. Windows
624	// start at 0, slide, 2*slide, ... and none with a negative start is created,
625	// so the first index is clamped to zero. The last index is
626	// eventTime/slide, so an event at a window end is outside that window.
627	type containingWindows struct {
628		count     int64 // how many windows contain the event time
629		lastStart int64 // start of the last (highest) containing window
630		slide     int64 // distance between consecutive window starts
631		// firstOverflow is the start of the earliest containing window whose end
632		// (start + windowMillis) leaves the signed 64-bit range, or -1 when every
633		// containing window fits. Containing starts are an ascending arithmetic
634		// sequence with step slide, so overflow (if any) is a suffix and this is
635		// its first member.
636		firstOverflow int64
637	}
638	
639	// containingWindows derives the containing-window range for eventTime.
640	func (s *aggregateState) containingWindows(eventTime int64) containingWindows {
641		last := eventTime / s.slideMillis
642		first := floorDiv(eventTime-s.windowMillis, s.slideMillis) + 1
643		if first < 0 {
644			first = 0
645		}
646		w := containingWindows{
647			count:         last - first + 1,
648			lastStart:     eventTime - eventTime%s.slideMillis,
649			slide:         s.slideMillis,
650			firstOverflow: -1,
651		}
652		lowest := w.start(w.count - 1) // earliest containing start; never negative
653		maxSafeStart := int64(math.MaxInt64 - s.windowMillis)
654		switch {
655		case lowest > maxSafeStart:
656			w.firstOverflow = lowest
657		default:
658			safe := (maxSafeStart-lowest)/s.slideMillis + 1 // containing starts that fit
659			if safe < w.count {
660				// Reach back from lastStart, which is at most eventTime, so the
661				// subtraction cannot leave the signed 64-bit range.
662				w.firstOverflow = w.start(w.count - 1 - safe)
663			}
664		}
665		return w
666	}
667	
668	// start returns the start of the containing window reached back by offset
669	// indices from the last one (offset 0 = last window).
670	func (w containingWindows) start(offset int64) int64 {
671		return w.lastStart - offset*w.slide
672	}
673	
674	// eventRecord is one input event whose record content has already been
675	// interpreted and validated independently of aggregate state: key, time,
676	// value and (in partitioned mode) partition are final. Nothing about idle
677	// partitions, watermarks or windows has been inspected yet, so producing one
678	// never mutates -- or even reads -- window state.
679	type eventRecord struct {
680		key       string
681		time      int64
682		value     int64
683		partition int64 // partitioned mode only; always 0 in legacy mode
684	}
685	
686	// parseEventRecord is the interpretation half of event intake. It reads and
687	// checks the record's own fields and never consults aggregate state, so field
688	// legality is fully decided before any idle, late or window rule runs. A
689	// repeated top-level "key" never reaches here: processLine rejects it before
690	// this call, so the fields are read exactly once each. Fields are validated
691	// in the order they have always been rejected: key, then time, then value,
692	// then partition. The key is decoded strictly: an empty key, invalid UTF-8
693	// bytes and an unpaired or mispaired surrogate half are record errors, never
694	// content repaired to U+FFFD that could merge keys. In legacy mode
695	// (partitioned == false) extra fields -- including any stray partition
696	// field -- stay ignored and partition is reported as zero.
697	func parseEventRecord(obj map[string]json.RawMessage, partitioned bool, partitionCount int64, lineNo int) (eventRecord, error) {
698		key, err := requiredKey(obj, lineNo)
699		if err != nil {
700			return eventRecord{}, err
701		}
702		if key == "" {
703			return eventRecord{}, &InputError{Line: lineNo, Reason: `field "key" must be a non-empty string`}
704		}
705		eventTime, err := requiredNonNegInt64(obj, "time", lineNo)
706		if err != nil {
707			return eventRecord{}, err
708		}
709		value, err := requiredInt64(obj, "value", lineNo)
710		if err != nil {
711			return eventRecord{}, err
712		}
713		var partition int64
714		if partitioned {
715			partition, err = requiredPartitionField(obj, partitionCount, lineNo)
716			if err != nil {
717				return eventRecord{}, err
718			}
719		}
720		return eventRecord{
721			key:       key,
722			time:      eventTime,
723			value:     value,
724			partition: partition,
725		}, nil
726	}
727	
728	func (s *aggregateState) processEvent(obj map[string]json.RawMessage, lineNo int) error {
729		// Stage 1: interpret and validate the record's own content without
730		// touching aggregate state.
731		ev, err := parseEventRecord(obj, s.partitions > 0, s.partitions, lineNo)
732		if err != nil {
733			return err
734		}
735		// Stage 2: apply the validated event to aggregate state.
736		return s.acceptEvent(ev, lineNo)
737	}
738	
739	// acceptEvent is the state half of event intake: it applies one record that
740	// parseEventRecord has already fully validated, in the same order as before
741	// the split -- idle partition first, then the global-watermark late rule, and
742	// only afterwards the window counts. It never re-reads or re-validates record
743	// fields, so a field problem can never be downgraded to an idle failure or a
744	// late notice here. Partitioned mode judges lateness against the overall
745	// effective watermark; an event on an idle partition stays fatal and never
746	// resumes the partition implicitly. A strictly late event is skipped with the
747	// existing notice; an event time equal to the watermark still enters its
748	// windows.
749	func (s *aggregateState) acceptEvent(ev eventRecord, lineNo int) error {
750		if s.partitions > 0 && s.idle[ev.partition] {
751			return &InputError{Line: lineNo, Reason: fmt.Sprintf("event for idle partition %d is not allowed; send a watermark to resume it first", ev.partition)}
752		}
753	
754		if s.watermark != nil && ev.time < *s.watermark {
755			notice := fmt.Sprintf("line %d: late event time=%d below current watermark %d, skipped\n", lineNo, ev.time, *s.watermark)
756			if err := writeFull(s.lateLog, []byte(notice)); err != nil {
757				return &OutputError{
758					Line:   lineNo,
759					Kind:   "late-event notice",
760					Detail: fmt.Sprintf("event time %d below current watermark %d", ev.time, *s.watermark),
761					Err:    err,
762				}
763			}
764			return nil
765		}
766	
767		return s.applyEventToWindows(ev, lineNo)
768	}
769	
770	// applyEventToWindows counts one accepted event in every window that contains
771	// its event time, one count and the full value per window. It only mutates
772	// window state; the caller has already settled field validity, idleness and
773	// lateness. The containing-window range is derived once and shared by the
774	// window-end overflow precheck and the counting loop, so both judge the exact
775	// same set of windows. The precheck runs before any window is touched;
776	// per-window count and sum overflows then fail on this triggering event in
777	// ascending window-start order rather than at watermark closure.
778	func (s *aggregateState) applyEventToWindows(ev eventRecord, lineNo int) error {
779		wins := s.containingWindows(ev.time)
780	
781		// A window whose end leaves the signed 64-bit range is fatal for the
782		// whole input line; check before updating any window state.
783		if wins.firstOverflow >= 0 {
784			return &InputError{Line: lineNo, Reason: fmt.Sprintf("window end overflow for key %q window starting at %d with length %d", ev.key, wins.firstOverflow, s.windowMillis)}
785		}
786	
787		// Add the event once to each containing window, in ascending start
788		// order. An overflow here stops processing immediately; already closed
789		// (and thus already written) windows are unaffected.
790		for i := wins.count - 1; i >= 0; i-- {
791			if err := s.addEventToWindow(ev, wins.start(i), lineNo); err != nil {
792				return err
793			}
794		}
795		return nil
796	}
797	
798	// addEventToWindow folds a single accepted event into one containing window,
799	// creating the window first if needed, enforcing the signed 64-bit count and
800	// cumulative-sum boundaries before the mutation. On failure the window keeps
801	// its previous count and sum and the error names the physical line, the key
802	// and this window's [start,end) interval.
803	func (s *aggregateState) addEventToWindow(ev eventRecord, start int64, lineNo int) error {
804		end := start + s.windowMillis
805		id := windowID{start: start, key: ev.key}
806		st := s.windows[id]
807		if st == nil {
808			st = &windowState{end: end}
809			s.windows[id] = st
810		}
811		if st.count == math.MaxInt64 {
812			return &InputError{Line: lineNo, Reason: fmt.Sprintf("event count overflow for key %q window [%d,%d)", ev.key, start, end)}
813		}
814		if ev.value > 0 && st.sum > math.MaxInt64-ev.value {
815			return &InputError{Line: lineNo, Reason: fmt.Sprintf("cumulative sum overflow for key %q window [%d,%d): %d + %d", ev.key, start, end, st.sum, ev.value)}
816		}
817		if ev.value < 0 && st.sum < math.MinInt64-ev.value {
818			return &InputError{Line: lineNo, Reason: fmt.Sprintf("cumulative sum overflow for key %q window [%d,%d): %d + %d", ev.key, start, end, st.sum, ev.value)}
819		}
820		st.count++
821		st.sum += ev.value
822		return nil
823	}

825	// watermarkRecord is one input watermark whose record content has already been
826	// interpreted and validated independently of aggregate state: time and (in
827	// partitioned mode) partition are final. Nothing about a previous watermark,
828	// the effective minimum or an idle partition has been inspected yet, so
829	// producing one never mutates -- or even reads -- window or watermark state.
830	type watermarkRecord struct {
831		time      int64
832		partition int64 // partitioned mode only; always 0 in legacy mode
833	}
834	
835	// parseWatermarkRecord is the interpretation half of watermark intake. It
836	// reads and checks the record's own fields and never consults aggregate
837	// state, so field legality is fully decided before any single-watermark,
838	// backwards or idle-resume rule runs. Fields are validated in the order they
839	// have always been rejected, independent of their textual order in the JSON:
840	// time first, then partition. Time must be a non-negative signed 64-bit
841	// integer. In partitioned mode partition must be present and in
842	// [0,partitionCount); when both fields are bad the time problem is the one
843	// reported. In legacy mode (partitioned == false) extra fields -- including
844	// any stray partition field, whatever its value -- stay ignored and never
845	// reject the record; partition is reported as zero.
846	func parseWatermarkRecord(obj map[string]json.RawMessage, partitioned bool, partitionCount int64, lineNo int) (watermarkRecord, error) {
847		next, err := requiredNonNegInt64(obj, "time", lineNo)
848		if err != nil {
849			return watermarkRecord{}, err
850		}
851		var partition int64
852		if partitioned {
853			partition, err = requiredPartitionField(obj, partitionCount, lineNo)
854			if err != nil {
855				return watermarkRecord{}, err
856			}
857		}
858		return watermarkRecord{time: next, partition: partition}, nil
859	}
860	
861	func (s *aggregateState) processWatermark(obj map[string]json.RawMessage, lineNo int) error {
862		// Stage 1: interpret and validate the record's own content without
863		// touching aggregate state.
864		wm, err := parseWatermarkRecord(obj, s.partitions > 0, s.partitions, lineNo)
865		if err != nil {
866			return err
867		}
868		// Stage 2: decide whether the validated watermark may change state and,
869		// only once it may, record it and close windows.
870		return s.acceptWatermark(wm, lineNo)
871	}
872	
873	// acceptWatermark is the state half of watermark intake: it applies one record
874	// that parseWatermarkRecord has already fully validated. It never re-reads or
875	// re-validates record fields, so a field problem can never be downgraded to a
876	// backwards-watermark or resume failure here, and a rejected record returns
877	// before any state changes: the partition is not resumed early, no watermark
878	// advances and no window output is triggered. A legal watermark may repeat or
879	// jump forward; the single legacy watermark and each active partition's own
880	// watermark still never move backwards. An accepted watermark funnels through
881	// the same advance-and-close path as an idle declaration.
882	func (s *aggregateState) acceptWatermark(wm watermarkRecord, lineNo int) error {
883		if s.partitions == 0 {
884			if s.watermark != nil && wm.time < *s.watermark {
885				return &InputError{Line: lineNo, Reason: fmt.Sprintf("watermark moved backwards from %d to %d", *s.watermark, wm.time)}
886			}
887			s.watermark = &wm.time
888			return s.advanceWatermark(lineNo)
889		}
890		if err := s.checkPartitionWatermark(wm, lineNo); err != nil {
891			return err
892		}
893		s.applyPartitionWatermark(wm)
894		return s.advanceWatermark(lineNo)
895	}
896	
897	// checkPartitionWatermark decides, without mutating anything, whether one
898	// record-valid partitioned-mode watermark may change aggregate state, and
899	// returns the existing *InputError when it may not. Two situations are kept
900	// apart:
901	//
902	//   - The partition is active: its watermark may repeat or jump forward but
903	//     never move backwards relative to its own previous value.
904	//   - The partition is idle: the record resumes it, and its time must be at
905	//     least both the partition's own previous watermark and the current
906	//     effective (minimum) watermark; equality on either boundary resumes. When
907	//     both lower bounds are violated the partition's own previous watermark is
908	//     the one reported, checked first. A partition that idled before ever
909	//     reporting has no previous watermark, so only the effective bound
910	//     applies.
911	func (s *aggregateState) checkPartitionWatermark(wm watermarkRecord, lineNo int) error {
912		p, next := wm.partition, wm.time
913		if s.idle[p] {
914			if prev, ok := s.partWatermark[p]; ok && next < *prev {
915				return &InputError{Line: lineNo, Reason: fmt.Sprintf("resume watermark %d for partition %d is below its previous watermark %d", next, p, *prev)}
916			}
917			if s.watermark != nil && next < *s.watermark {
918				return &InputError{Line: lineNo, Reason: fmt.Sprintf("resume watermark %d for partition %d is below the current effective watermark %d", next, p, *s.watermark)}
919			}
920			return nil
921		}
922		if prev, ok := s.partWatermark[p]; ok && next < *prev {
923			return &InputError{Line: lineNo, Reason: fmt.Sprintf("watermark for partition %d moved backwards from %d to %d", p, *prev, next)}
924		}
925		return nil
926	}
927	
928	// applyPartitionWatermark records one partition watermark that
929	// checkPartitionWatermark has already accepted, keeping the bookkeeping apart
930	// from the decision: a resume removes the partition from the idle set, and the
931	// first report from an active partition decrements the count of partitions
932	// the effective watermark still waits for. A resume of a never-reported
933	// partition changes no counter -- that partition was already subtracted when
934	// it was declared idle -- and only after that is the partition's watermark
935	// value replaced.
936	func (s *aggregateState) applyPartitionWatermark(wm watermarkRecord) {
937		p, next := wm.partition, wm.time
938		resuming := s.idle[p]
939		if resuming {
940			delete(s.idle, p)
941		}
942		if _, reported := s.partWatermark[p]; !reported && !resuming {
943			s.unreportedActive--
944		}
945		s.partWatermark[p] = &next
946	}
947	
948	// processIdle declares a partition idle: it stops contributing to the
949	// effective watermark until its next watermark record. The declaration
950	// itself may advance the effective watermark and close windows.
951	func (s *aggregateState) processIdle(obj map[string]json.RawMessage, lineNo int) error {
952		p, err := s.requiredPartition(obj, lineNo)
953		if err != nil {
954			return err
955		}
956		if s.idle[p] {
957			// A repeated idle declaration is a no-op: the partition already
958			// stopped contributing, so neither the effective watermark nor the
959			// set of closable windows can change.
960			return nil
961		}
962		s.idle[p] = true
963		if _, reported := s.partWatermark[p]; !reported {
964			// An unreported partition that goes idle stops being waited on: one
965			// fewer active partition the effective watermark still needs.
966			s.unreportedActive--
967		}
968		// With the partition excluded, the remaining non-idle partitions
969		// determine the effective watermark; the declaration itself can advance
970		// it and close windows, exactly like a watermark update.
971		return s.advanceWatermark(lineNo)
972	}
973	
974	// advanceWatermark applies a partition state change -- a partition watermark
975	// update or an idle declaration -- and closes every window the resulting
976	// watermark allows. Both triggers funnel through here so they follow the
977	// same rules: in partitioned mode the effective watermark is recomputed from
978	// the current partition state (an active partition that has not reported yet
979	// keeps it unknown, and when every partition is idle the last produced value
980	// is retained instead of clearing); in legacy single-watermark mode the
981	// single watermark is used as is. While no effective watermark exists no
982	// window closes; otherwise closeWindows emits every window whose end is less
983	// than or equal to it.
984	func (s *aggregateState) advanceWatermark(lineNo int) error {
985		if s.partitions > 0 {
986			if next := s.effectiveWatermark(); next != nil {
987				s.watermark = next
988			}
989		}
990		if s.watermark == nil {
991			return nil
992		}
993		return s.closeWindows(*s.watermark, lineNo)
994	}
995	
996	// effectiveWatermark returns the minimum watermark over the non-idle
997	// partitions once each of them has reported at least once, or nil
998	// otherwise. When every partition is idle, nil is returned so the caller
999	// keeps the last produced effective watermark. The waiting check itself is
1000	// the unreportedActive counter, maintained incrementally as partitions
1001	// report or go idle, so a watermark or idle record that arrives while
1002	// partitions are still silent costs one comparison rather than a rescan of
1003	// every partition's reporting state; only once the counter reaches zero --
1004	// every active partition has reported -- is the minimum computed by the
1005	// scan below, exactly as before.
1006	func (s *aggregateState) effectiveWatermark() *int64 {
1007		active := s.partitions - int64(len(s.idle))
1008		if active <= 0 || s.unreportedActive > 0 {
1009			return nil
1010		}
1011		var min int64
1012		first := true
1013		for p := int64(0); p < s.partitions; p++ {
1014			if s.idle[p] {
1015				continue
1016			}
1017			w, ok := s.partWatermark[p]
1018			if !ok {
1019				return nil
1020			}
1021			if first || *w < min {
1022				min = *w
1023				first = false
1024			}
1025		}
1026		return &min
1027	}
1028	
1029	// requiredPartition returns the record's partition index. In legacy mode it
1030	// returns 0 without inspecting the record, so extra fields stay ignored. In
1031	// partitioned mode the actual reading and range checking lives in the shared
1032	// free function used by event interpretation as well.
1033	func (s *aggregateState) requiredPartition(obj map[string]json.RawMessage, lineNo int) (int64, error) {
1034		if s.partitions == 0 {
1035			return 0, nil
1036		}
1037		return requiredPartitionField(obj, s.partitions, lineNo)
1038	}
1039	
1040	// requiredPartitionField reads and range-checks a partitioned-mode record's
1041	// "partition" field. It is pure record interpretation: the partition count is
1042	// passed in rather than read from aggregate state, so both the event intake
1043	// split (parseEventRecord) and the watermark/idle paths validate the field by
1044	// the exact same rule without touching window state.
1045	func requiredPartitionField(obj map[string]json.RawMessage, partitionCount int64, lineNo int) (int64, error) {
1046		p, err := requiredInt64(obj, "partition", lineNo)
1047		if err != nil {
1048			return 0, err
1049		}
1050		if p < 0 || p >= partitionCount {
1051			return 0, &InputError{Line: lineNo, Reason: fmt.Sprintf("field %q must be an integer in range [0,%d), got %d", "partition", partitionCount, p)}
1052		}
1053		return p, nil
1054	}

1056	func (s *aggregateState) closeWindows(watermark int64, lineNo int) error {
1057		type pending struct {
1058			id windowID
1059			st *windowState
1060		}
1061		var ready []pending
1062		for id, st := range s.windows {
1063			if st.end <= watermark {
1064				ready = append(ready, pending{id: id, st: st})
1065			}
1066		}
1067		sort.Slice(ready, func(i, j int) bool {
1068			if ready[i].st.end != ready[j].st.end {
1069				return ready[i].st.end < ready[j].st.end
1070			}
1071			return ready[i].id.key < ready[j].id.key
1072		})
1073		for _, p := range ready {
1074			encoded, err := json.Marshal(AggregateResult{
1075				Key:   p.id.key,
1076				Start: p.id.start,
1077				End:   p.st.end,
1078				Count: p.st.count,
1079				Sum:   p.st.sum,
1080			})
1081			if err != nil {
1082				return err
1083			}
1084			line := append(encoded, '\n')
1085			if err := writeFull(s.out, line); err != nil {
1086				// Stop immediately: the writer may hold zero bytes or only a
1087				// prefix of this record, but a truncated record is not a fully
1088				// output one, so the window stays open in the map. Do not retry
1089				// or resend it and do not emit the remaining ready windows;
1090				// content already accepted by the writer stays.
1091				return &OutputError{
1092					Line:   lineNo,
1093					Kind:   "window result",
1094					Detail: fmt.Sprintf("key %q window [%d,%d)", p.id.key, p.id.start, p.st.end),
1095					Err:    err,
1096				}
1097			}
1098			delete(s.windows, p.id)
1099		}
1100		return nil
1101	}

1103	func requiredString(obj map[string]json.RawMessage, field string, lineNo int) (string, error) {
1104		raw, ok := obj[field]
1105		if !ok {
1106			return "", &InputError{Line: lineNo, Reason: fmt.Sprintf("missing required string field %q", field)}
1107		}
1108		value, err := decodeString(raw, field)
1109		if err != nil {
1110			return "", &InputError{Line: lineNo, Reason: err.Error()}
1111		}
1112		return value, nil
1113	}
1114	
1115	// requiredKey returns the event key decoded strictly. encoding/json silently
1116	// repairs damaged string content with U+FFFD -- invalid UTF-8 bytes and \u
1117	// escapes whose surrogate halves are unpaired or mispaired -- which would
1118	// merge distinct damaged keys into one and collide with a key that is
1119	// genuinely U+FFFD. Such damage is a fatal input error here instead, so a
1120	// corrupt key never changes any window's count or sum. Valid characters
1121	// (including a directly encoded or escaped U+FFFD and supplementary-plane
1122	// characters, whether literal or written as a surrogate pair) decode to
1123	// their exact value and aggregate as before.
1124	func requiredKey(obj map[string]json.RawMessage, lineNo int) (string, error) {
1125		raw, ok := obj["key"]
1126		if !ok {
1127			return "", &InputError{Line: lineNo, Reason: `missing required string field "key"`}
1128		}
1129		key, err := decodeKeyString(raw)
1130		if err != nil {
1131			return "", &InputError{Line: lineNo, Reason: err.Error()}
1132		}
1133		return key, nil
1134	}
1135	
1136	// decodeKeyString decodes the event key's JSON string without the lossy
1137	// repairs encoding/json applies: invalid UTF-8 byte sequences and \u escapes
1138	// with unpaired or mispaired surrogate halves are errors instead of becoming
1139	// U+FFFD. The record already parsed as JSON, so the string's escape syntax
1140	// is valid; only its character content is checked here. An escaped backslash
1141	// is decoded first, so "\\uD800" stays the literal text D800 and is not
1142	// mistaken for an unpaired surrogate.
1143	func decodeKeyString(raw json.RawMessage) (string, error) {
1144		trimmed := bytes.TrimSpace(raw)
1145		if len(trimmed) < 2 || trimmed[0] != '"' || trimmed[len(trimmed)-1] != '"' {
1146			return "", fmt.Errorf("field %q must be a JSON string, got %s", "key", string(trimmed))
1147		}
1148		s := string(trimmed[1 : len(trimmed)-1])
1149		var sb strings.Builder
1150		sb.Grow(len(s))
1151		for i := 0; i < len(s); {
1152			c := s[i]
1153			switch {
1154			case c == '\\':
1155				if i+1 >= len(s) {
1156					return "", fmt.Errorf("field %q ends in an incomplete escape", "key")
1157				}
1158				switch s[i+1] {
1159				case '"', '\\', '/':
1160					sb.WriteByte(s[i+1])
1161					i += 2
1162				case 'b':
1163					sb.WriteByte('\b')
1164					i += 2
1165				case 'f':
1166					sb.WriteByte('\f')
1167					i += 2
1168				case 'n':
1169					sb.WriteByte('\n')
1170					i += 2
1171				case 'r':
1172					sb.WriteByte('\r')
1173					i += 2
1174				case 't':
1175					sb.WriteByte('\t')
1176					i += 2
1177				case 'u':
1178					r, next, err := decodeUnicodeEscape(s, i)
1179					if err != nil {
1180						return "", err
1181					}
1182					sb.WriteRune(r)
1183					i = next
1184				default:
1185					return "", fmt.Errorf("field %q has an invalid escape \\%c", "key", s[i+1])
1186				}
1187			case c < utf8.RuneSelf:
1188				sb.WriteByte(c)
1189				i++
1190			default:
1191				r, size := utf8.DecodeRuneInString(s[i:])
1192				if r == utf8.RuneError && size == 1 {
1193					return "", fmt.Errorf("field %q contains invalid UTF-8 bytes in its character encoding", "key")
1194				}
1195				sb.WriteString(s[i : i+size])
1196				i += size
1197			}
1198		}
1199		return sb.String(), nil
1200	}
1201	
1202	// decodeUnicodeEscape decodes the \uXXXX escape at s[i] (where s[i] == '\\'
1203	// and s[i+1] == 'u'), returning the decoded rune and the index just past the
1204	// escape. A high surrogate must be immediately followed by a \u escape
1205	// carrying the matching low surrogate; the pair combines into one
1206	// supplementary-plane rune. An unpaired or mispaired half is an error rather
1207	// than U+FFFD.
1208	func decodeUnicodeEscape(s string, i int) (rune, int, error) {
1209		r, next, err := parseHexEscape(s, i)
1210		if err != nil {
1211			return 0, 0, err
1212		}
1213		switch {
1214		case r >= 0xD800 && r <= 0xDBFF:
1215			if next+1 >= len(s) || s[next] != '\\' || s[next+1] != 'u' {
1216				return 0, 0, fmt.Errorf("field %q has an unpaired high surrogate in a Unicode escape", "key")
1217			}
1218			lo, after, err := parseHexEscape(s, next)
1219			if err != nil {
1220				return 0, 0, err
1221			}
1222			if lo < 0xDC00 || lo > 0xDFFF {
1223				return 0, 0, fmt.Errorf("field %q has a high surrogate not followed by a low surrogate in a Unicode escape", "key")
1224			}
1225			return 0x10000 + (r-0xD800)<<10 + (lo - 0xDC00), after, nil
1226		case r >= 0xDC00 && r <= 0xDFFF:
1227			return 0, 0, fmt.Errorf("field %q has an unpaired low surrogate in a Unicode escape", "key")
1228		}
1229		return r, next, nil
1230	}
1231	
1232	// parseHexEscape reads the four hex digits of the \uXXXX escape at s[i]
1233	// (where s[i] == '\\' and s[i+1] == 'u') and returns their value and the
1234	// index just past them.
1235	func parseHexEscape(s string, i int) (rune, int, error) {
1236		if i+6 > len(s) {
1237			return 0, 0, fmt.Errorf("field %q has a truncated Unicode escape", "key")
1238		}
1239		var v rune
1240		for _, c := range s[i+2 : i+6] {
1241			v <<= 4
1242			switch {
1243			case c >= '0' && c <= '9':
1244				v += c - '0'
1245			case c >= 'a' && c <= 'f':
1246				v += c - 'a' + 10
1247			case c >= 'A' && c <= 'F':
1248				v += c - 'A' + 10
1249			default:
1250				return 0, 0, fmt.Errorf("field %q has a non-hex digit in a Unicode escape", "key")
1251			}
1252		}
1253		return v, i + 6, nil
1254	}

1256	func requiredInt64(obj map[string]json.RawMessage, field string, lineNo int) (int64, error) {
1257		raw, ok := obj[field]

1260		}

func runAggregate(args []string) int {
	fs := flag.NewFlagSet("aggregate", flag.ContinueOnError)
	fs.SetOutput(os.Stderr)
	fs.Usage = func() {
		fmt.Fprintln(fs.Output(), "usage: edgefleet aggregate --window-ms <milliseconds> [--slide-ms <milliseconds>] [--partitions <count>]")
		fmt.Fprintln(fs.Output(), `run "edgefleet help" for the full record and window closure rules`)
	}
	windowMillis := fs.Int64("window-ms", 0, "window length in milliseconds (required, positive signed 64-bit integer)")
	slideMillis := fs.Int64("slide-ms", 0, "distance between consecutive window starts in milliseconds (optional positive signed 64-bit integer, no greater than --window-ms); defaults to the window length for non-overlapping fixed windows")
	partitions := fs.Int64("partitions", 0, "number of input partitions (optional positive signed 64-bit integer); when set, every record must carry an integer partition in [0,count)")
	if err := fs.Parse(args); err != nil {
		return 2
	}
	if fs.NArg() != 0 {
		fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "aggregate accepts no positional arguments, got %v\n", fs.Args())
		fs.Usage()
		return 2
	}
	windowSpecified := false
	slideSpecified := false
	partitionsSpecified := false
	fs.Visit(func(f *flag.Flag) {
		switch f.Name {
		case "window-ms":
			windowSpecified = true
		case "slide-ms":
			slideSpecified = true
		case "partitions":
			partitionsSpecified = true
		}
	})
	if !windowSpecified {
		fmt.Fprintln(os.Stderr, "aggregate requires --window-ms <milliseconds>")
		fs.Usage()
		return 2
	}
	// An omitted --slide-ms defaults to the window length (fixed windows).
	// This is an omission policy specific to the command: an explicitly given
	// zero is left untouched, so it is still rejected below rather than being
	// silently treated as the default.
	if !slideSpecified {
		*slideMillis = *windowMillis
	}
	// The numeric limits are shared with the library entry points and live in
	// edgefleet.ValidateAggregateParams; only the flag-named wording and exit
	// code are command-specific. The shared report order (window, slide,
	// slide-vs-window, partitions) is the order this command already used.
	if err := edgefleet.ValidateAggregateParams(*windowMillis, *slideMillis, *partitions); err != nil {
		var paramErr *edgefleet.AggregateParamError
		if errors.As(err, &paramErr) {
			fmt.Fprint(os.Stderr, aggregateParamCLIError(paramErr))
		} else {
			fmt.Fprintln(os.Stderr, "aggregate:", err)
		}
		return 2
	}
	// The command rejects an explicitly supplied non-positive --partitions;
	// the library accepts zero as its legacy single-watermark mode selector.
	// The shared validator already rejected negative counts, so here this only
	// catches an explicit zero, kept as the command's own policy.
	if partitionsSpecified && *partitions <= 0 {
		fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "aggregate --partitions must be a positive signed 64-bit integer, got %d\n", *partitions)
		return 2
	}
	var err error
	if partitionsSpecified {
		err = edgefleet.RunAggregatePartitionedSliding(os.Stdin, *windowMillis, *slideMillis, *partitions, os.Stdout, os.Stderr)
	} else {
		err = edgefleet.RunAggregateSliding(os.Stdin, *windowMillis, *slideMillis, os.Stdout, os.Stderr)
	}
	if err != nil {
		fmt.Fprintln(os.Stderr, "aggregate:", err)
		return 1
	}
	return 0
}

// aggregateParamCLIError renders a shared *edgefleet.AggregateParamError in
// the command's existing flag-named wording. The limit and its checking order
// come from edgefleet.ValidateAggregateParams; only this text and the exit
// code are command-specific.
func aggregateParamCLIError(e *edgefleet.AggregateParamError) string {
	switch e.Kind {
	case edgefleet.AggregateParamTooLarge:
		return fmt.Sprintf("aggregate --slide-ms %d must not exceed --window-ms %d\n", e.Value, e.Limit)
	case edgefleet.AggregateParamNotPositive:
		switch e.Field {
		case edgefleet.AggregateParamWindow:
			return fmt.Sprintf("aggregate --window-ms must be a positive signed 64-bit integer, got %d\n", e.Value)
		case edgefleet.AggregateParamSlide:
			return fmt.Sprintf("aggregate --slide-ms must be a positive signed 64-bit integer, got %d\n", e.Value)
		case edgefleet.AggregateParamPartitions:
			return fmt.Sprintf("aggregate --partitions must be a positive signed 64-bit integer, got %d\n", e.Value)
		}
	}
	return fmt.Sprintf("aggregate: invalid %s parameter %d\n", e.Field, e.Value)
}
